root.name: Benoni Defense: Pawn Storm Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 c5 3. d5 e6 4. Nc3 exd5 5. cxd5 d6 6. e4 g6 7. f4

overview: The Four Pawns Attack: White builds the broadest centre with pawns on d5, e4 and f4 and threatens e4-e5. Black replies 7...Bg7 8.Nf3 O-O and strikes at the centre with ...Re8 and ...Nbd7 (or ...c4 ideas later), aiming at the e4 pawn and the e5 square. White plays Be2, O-O and e5 to open lines for the pieces before Black's counterplay on the e-file and queenside arrives. The game is concrete and tactical, with a lot of known theory.

white_ideas.idea: Push e4-e5 to break open the centre while Black's king is still in the middle of development
Hold the space with d5, e4, f4 and play on the kingside with Bd3, Nf3, O-O
Meet ...Re8 and ...c4 with accurate piece placement; Bb5+ ideas

black_ideas.idea: Strike at e4 with ...Re8, ...Nbd7 and ...Nh5 or ...Ng4 to stop e5
Fianchetto with ...Bg7 and later ...Bg4 or ...Qh4+ ideas
Queenside play with ...a6, ...b5 once the centre is stable

typical_structures.structure: Modern Benoni with White d5, e4, f4 against Black c5, d6, g6; half-open e-file for Black

character.notes: Dangerous central expansion vs counterattack; one inaccurate move loses quickly. Sharp.

gambit.notes: No material is given; Black's ...b5 gambit ideas occur only later.

soundness.notes: Black's set-up is sound but theory is demanding; the line has been called one of White's most dangerous.

structure.notes: Fixed asymmetric centre: White d5/e4/f4 vs Black c5/d6, with a half-open e-file for Black. Semi-open, though it plays closed until e5.

approach.notes: A main-line White reply to the Benoni, played at every level. Standard.

level.notes: Black must know the e5 break and the move orders in detail; Advanced.

sublines_that_differ.name: Four Pawns with 8.Nf3
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 c5 3. d5 e6 4. Nc3 exd5 5. cxd5 d6 6. e4 g6 7. f4 Bg7 8. Nf3
sublines_that_differ.how: Main continuation; Black castles and chooses between ...Re8 and ...c4 pushes.

sublines_that_differ.name: Taimanov Attack
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 c5 3. d5 e6 4. Nc3 exd5 5. cxd5 d6 6. e4 g6 7. f4 Bg7 8. Bb5+
sublines_that_differ.how: White forces a bishop check to disrupt Black's development.

character.reason: White's pawn mass attacks at once and Black must find precise counter-strikes.

gambit.reason: No material is offered in the main lines.

soundness.reason: Four Pawns is a respected main-line try and Black's defence is accepted.

structure.reason: Fixed asymmetric centre with a half-open e-file for Black, like the Sicilian pattern; it could be read as Closed.

approach.reason: A main-line attack against the Benoni played by strong players.

level.reason: Sharp, heavily theoretical lines with precise timing for Black.

plans.reason: White's d5/e4/f4 pawn mass aims for e5 and central control.
